newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel warns budget deficit demands action.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel warns budget deficit demands action.

text.p: The Israeli government's large budget deficit in June should be taken as a warning to the Treasury to cut spending immediately, the Bank of Israel said in a statement on Wednesday.
"Raising confidence in budgetary policy is especially important after two years during which major deviations occurred in the state budget," the central bank said.
"Continuous monitoring of the deficit and adjusting the budget as needed...are important to ensure the economy returns to a path of continuous growth," the bank said.
On Tuesday, the Treasury reported a June deficit of 3.14 billion shekels, by far the biggest monthly deficit this year.
In the first half the deficit amounted to 4.8 billion shekels, against a deficit target for all of 1997 of 9.7 billion shekels, equal to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.

The deficit is usually high in June, boosted by interest payments on government loans and by a bonus paid to civil servants during the month. Nevertheless, Treasury officials had been expecting a smaller deficit.

The Treasury has proposed budget cuts of up to 600 million shekels to help met this year's deficit target, but the matter has not been brought before the cabinet. Dan Meridor, who quit as finance minister June 18, has not been replaced.
